URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/14/uk-health-secretary-wes-streeting-resigns-from-government

Wes Streeting resigned as Britain's health secretary on Thursday 14 May 2026, posting on X that he no longer had "confidence" in Sir Keir Starmer's leadership.

Streeting quote: "It is now clear that you will not lead the Labour Party into the next general election"

Streeting did not explicitly declare a formal leadership challenge in his resignation. He did not confirm whether he had secured the support of 81 MPs (one fifth of Labour MPs) needed to trigger a formal leadership contest under Labour rules.

He is the first Cabinet member to resign in this crisis.

Four junior ministers had already resigned earlier this week, including Safeguarding Minister Jess Phillips.

More than 80 Labour MPs have called for Starmer to quit or outline departure plans.

Streeting is popular with Labour's right wing but opposed by left-wing members.

Starmer's response (via spokesman): the Prime Minister "is purely focused on governing" and is "getting on with the job" — indicating he will not step aside.

Finance Minister (Chancellor) Rachel Reeves urged Labour colleagues not to risk the economy through a leadership challenge.

Despite mounting pressure, no MP has formally challenged Starmer for his position at the time of publication.
